megaMenu.unsureBody: Tell us your crop and your hectares and we will map the flight calendar around them.

home.headlineTwo: Stop treating it like it isn't.

home.statFlight: to fly {hectares} hectares at {resolution} cm per pixel.

home.loopTitle: Scan the block. Mark the problem. Treat the marks.
home.loopLede: Every capability here is a version of the same loop. What changes is the sensor on the aircraft and what the model is looking for.

home.treatBody: Findings become zones and zones become a prescription your sprayer, spreader or hoe loads directly. Nothing outside a zone is touched.
home.bentoTitle: Eighteen jobs a drone does better than a walk

footer.blurb: Drone scouting, treatment maps and the flights that produce them. You book the calendar, we bring the aircraft, the pilots and the paperwork.
footer.disclaimer: Figures shown on this site come from a modelled demonstration field, labelled as such wherever they appear. Aerial application of plant protection products is restricted under EU and German law; our maps are built for the machines already permitted to apply them.

contact.title: Bring us one field and we will fly it
contact.lede: We walk the block with you, agree what is worth looking for, and fly it. You read the report before anyone talks about a calendar.
contact.step1: We call within two working days
contact.step1Body: Enough to understand the rotation and whether we can fly where you are.
contact.step2: We walk one block with you
contact.step2Body: Pick the field that has been annoying you. That is the one worth flying first.
contact.step3Body: Problem areas, recommendations, and a prescription if the capability produces one.
contact.writeInstead: Would you rather write to a person?
contact.name: Your name
contact.nameHelp: So we know who we are calling.
contact.message: What is the field that annoys you
contact.privacy: We use this to reply and to plan the visit. Nothing else, and nobody else.

booked.title: Booked. We will be in touch.
booked.body: Someone will call within two working days to agree which block to walk first. Pick the field that has been annoying you: that is the one worth flying.

subscribed.title: You are on the list.
subscribed.body: The next set of field notes will come to that address: what the flights are finding, and when the windows open. A few times a season, nothing else. Every one carries an unsubscribe link.

targeted-weed-control.name: Targeted weed control
targeted-weed-control.tagline: Spray the weeds, not the field
targeted-weed-control.summary: Cameras and on-board models find weeds plant by plant, then only the affected square metres get treated.
targeted-weed-control.problem: Blanket spraying treats the whole field because nobody knows which parts actually carry weeds. On a typical arable field the weed pressure is patchy: dense along headlands and tramlines, thin across the middle. Every litre applied to clean ground is money spent, residue added, and resistance pressure built for no agronomic return.
targeted-weed-control.cadence: Two to four scouting flights per crop, timed to the herbicide windows.
targeted-weed-control.readings.0: Treated area as a share of field area
targeted-weed-control.readings.3: Zone count and mean zone size
targeted-weed-control.steps.0.title: Scan
targeted-weed-control.steps.0.text: The drone flies a fixed grid at low altitude and photographs the canopy at centimetre resolution.
targeted-weed-control.steps.1.title: Classify
targeted-weed-control.steps.1.text: An on-board model separates crop from weed and tags each detection with a species guess and a confidence score.
targeted-weed-control.steps.2.title: Map
targeted-weed-control.steps.2.text: Detections are clustered into treatment zones and written to a prescription map with a buffer you set.
targeted-weed-control.steps.3.title: Treat
targeted-weed-control.steps.3.text: The map loads into your section-control sprayer or spot-spray rig, which opens nozzles only over the marked zones.

plant-disease-detection.name: Early disease detection
plant-disease-detection.tagline: See the infection before the eye can
plant-disease-detection.summary: Multispectral imaging picks up stress, fungal infection and nutrient shortfall days before symptoms are visible from the cab.
plant-disease-detection.problem: By the time a farmer sees a disease from the tractor seat, the infection has usually been established for a week or more and the treatment window has narrowed to a curative spray instead of a protective one. Walking the field catches it earlier, but nobody has the hours to walk every hectare weekly.
plant-disease-detection.cadence: Weekly through the main growth stages, tightening around high risk weather.
plant-disease-detection.outputs.1: Change layer against the previous flight
plant-disease-detection.readings.3: Days from flag to ground truth
plant-disease-detection.steps.0.title: Capture
plant-disease-detection.steps.0.text: A multispectral camera records red edge and near infrared bands alongside visible light.
plant-disease-detection.steps.1.title: Index
plant-disease-detection.steps.1.text: The bands are combined into vegetation indices that expose chlorophyll loss and cell structure damage.
plant-disease-detection.steps.2.title: Compare
plant-disease-detection.steps.2.text: Each flight is compared against the field's own history, so a wet spring baseline does not read as disease.
plant-disease-detection.steps.3.title: Flag
plant-disease-detection.steps.3.text: Divergent patches are ranked by severity and area, with a scouting route so you can ground truth the worst first.

pest-monitoring.name: Automated pest monitoring
pest-monitoring.summary: Regular flights check fields for pest damage and mark the affected areas on a map you can act on.
pest-monitoring.problem: Pest scouting is sampling: a handful of spots per field, a few times a season, and the rest is inference. Outbreaks that start in a corner get found when they have already spread, and the response is a whole field treatment because the actual extent was never mapped.
pest-monitoring.cadence: Every three to seven days during the risk window for your crop.
pest-monitoring.readings.2: Time from first detection to alert
pest-monitoring.steps.0.title: Patrol
pest-monitoring.steps.0.text: The same route is flown on a fixed schedule so every flight is comparable with the last.
pest-monitoring.steps.1.title: Detect
pest-monitoring.steps.1.text: Feeding damage, lodging and canopy holes are picked out of the imagery and located to the square metre.
pest-monitoring.steps.2.title: Track
pest-monitoring.steps.2.text: Each affected area gets an identity and is followed across flights, so growth or collapse is visible.
pest-monitoring.steps.3.title: Alert
pest-monitoring.steps.3.text: When an area crosses the threshold you set, the alert lands on your phone with the map already drawn.

precision-fertilisation.name: Precision fertilisation
precision-fertilisation.tagline: Feed the rows that are short
precision-fertilisation.summary: The system works out which parts of the crop are under-supplied and builds a variable rate map for the spreader.
precision-fertilisation.problem: A flat application rate assumes the field is uniform. It is not. Headlands, old field boundaries, sandy patches and wet hollows each take up nitrogen differently, so a single rate simultaneously overfeeds the strong areas and starves the weak ones. The overfed parts lodge and leach; the starved parts cost yield.
precision-fertilisation.cadence: Before each split application, typically two to three times per season.
precision-fertilisation.readings.0: Total product planned versus flat rate
precision-fertilisation.steps.0.title: Measure
precision-fertilisation.steps.0.text: Multispectral flights produce a biomass and chlorophyll picture of the standing crop.
precision-fertilisation.steps.1.title: Zone
precision-fertilisation.steps.1.text: The field is divided into management zones that follow the actual pattern, not a grid drawn on top of it.
precision-fertilisation.steps.2.title: Prescribe
precision-fertilisation.steps.2.text: Each zone gets a rate derived from your target, your soil samples and the measured shortfall.
precision-fertilisation.steps.3.title: Apply
precision-fertilisation.steps.3.text: The prescription exports to your spreader or applicator in the format your terminal expects.

irrigation-analysis.name: Irrigation analysis
irrigation-analysis.tagline: Find the dry corner and the buried leak
irrigation-analysis.summary: Thermal imaging exposes dry patches, leaks and uneven coverage so water goes where it is actually needed.
irrigation-analysis.problem: Irrigation problems are invisible until the crop shows them, and by then the water has already been wasted. A partially blocked nozzle, a slow leak in a buried line, or a pivot that under-delivers on one arc can run for weeks while the meter keeps counting.
irrigation-analysis.cadence: Fortnightly during the irrigation season, plus a check flight after any repair.
irrigation-analysis.steps.0.title: Fly warm
irrigation-analysis.steps.0.text: Thermal flights are timed for the hottest part of the day, when water stressed plants separate most clearly from watered ones.
irrigation-analysis.steps.1.title: Normalise
irrigation-analysis.steps.1.text: Canopy temperature is corrected against air temperature and reference surfaces so readings compare across days.
irrigation-analysis.steps.2.title: Locate
irrigation-analysis.steps.2.text: Cold anomalies point to leaks and pooling; hot anomalies point to under-delivery and stress.
irrigation-analysis.steps.3.title: Route
irrigation-analysis.steps.3.text: Each anomaly becomes a marked point with coordinates you can walk or drive to directly.

yield-forecasting.name: Yield forecasting
yield-forecasting.tagline: Count what is actually out there
yield-forecasting.summary: Drones count plants, fruit or ears and turn the counts into a yield estimate for each part of the field.
yield-forecasting.problem: Harvest planning, storage booking and forward selling all run on an estimate, and the estimate usually comes from a hand count in a few square metres extrapolated across a hundred hectares. A bad estimate books the wrong number of trailers and sells grain that is not there.
yield-forecasting.cadence: Once at establishment, then at two or three points through grain fill or fruit set.
yield-forecasting.outputs.0: Plant or fruit count per zone
yield-forecasting.readings.2: Gap area as a share of the field
yield-forecasting.steps.0.title: Fly low
yield-forecasting.steps.0.text: A high resolution pass captures individual plants, ears or fruit at a density the model can count.
yield-forecasting.steps.1.title: Count
yield-forecasting.steps.1.text: Objects are counted per square metre and the counts are aggregated by zone rather than averaged flat.
yield-forecasting.steps.2.title: Model
yield-forecasting.steps.2.text: Counts are combined with your variety, row spacing and historical yields to produce an estimate range.
yield-forecasting.steps.3.title: Update
yield-forecasting.steps.3.text: The forecast is re-run on each later flight, so the range narrows as harvest approaches.

field-mapping.name: Automated field mapping
field-mapping.tagline: The base layer everything else sits on
field-mapping.summary: One flight produces a high resolution 3D model of the field: elevation, drainage lines, headlands and problem ground.
field-mapping.problem: Most farms are still working from a field boundary drawn once and a memory of where the wet spot is. Without an elevation model there is no way to see why one corner floods, where the water actually runs, or how much of a field is not worth cropping at all.
field-mapping.cadence: Once per field, then refreshed after drainage work or a boundary change.
field-mapping.sensors.2: Downward LiDAR on wooded or tall canopy blocks
field-mapping.readings.3: Boundary area against the registered area
field-mapping.steps.0.title: Survey
field-mapping.steps.0.text: The drone flies an overlapping photogrammetry grid over the whole block.
field-mapping.steps.1.title: Reconstruct
field-mapping.steps.1.text: Images are matched into a point cloud, then a surface model and an orthophoto.
field-mapping.steps.2.title: Derive
field-mapping.steps.2.text: Slope, aspect, flow accumulation and depressions are calculated from the surface.
field-mapping.steps.3.title: Publish
field-mapping.steps.3.text: Layers are written to your field record so every later flight is measured against the same base.

wildlife-rescue.name: Wildlife detection before mowing
wildlife-rescue.tagline: Find the fawn before the mower does
wildlife-rescue.summary: Thermal drones search grassland ahead of the mower for fawns, hares and ground nesting birds, and mark every find.
wildlife-rescue.problem: Roe deer leave their fawns lying in tall grass, and a fawn's instinct is to press flat rather than run. The first cut of silage every spring kills a large number of them. In Germany the responsibility to take reasonable precautions sits with the person doing the mowing, and walking a field with a line of helpers rarely covers it in the time available.
wildlife-rescue.cadence: Every first cut, and any later cut on fields with known activity.
wildlife-rescue.outputs.0: Live find map on the ground crew's phone
wildlife-rescue.outputs.3: Season summary for the hunting tenant
wildlife-rescue.readings.2: Search completed before the mower started
wildlife-rescue.steps.0.title: Fly at dawn
wildlife-rescue.steps.0.text: The search runs in the cool hours before mowing, when a warm body contrasts most strongly with the sward.
wildlife-rescue.steps.1.title: Detect heat
wildlife-rescue.steps.1.text: The thermal camera picks out warm shapes and the model separates animals from stones, molehills and machinery.
wildlife-rescue.steps.2.title: Mark
wildlife-rescue.steps.2.text: Every find is pinned to a coordinate and pushed live to the phone of the person on the ground.
wildlife-rescue.steps.3.title: Clear
wildlife-rescue.steps.3.text: The animal is carried out or boxed, the point is closed off in the app, and the mower follows behind the cleared area.

drone-seeding.name: Drone seeding
drone-seeding.tagline: Sow where the drill cannot go
drone-seeding.summary: Drones broadcast seed and seed pods onto ground that is too steep, too wet or too awkward for a machine.
drone-seeding.problem: Cover crops go in late because the drill cannot get on wet stubble. Steep banks, wet hollows and awkward corners are either skipped or damaged by a machine that should not have been there. Reseeding a washed out patch means bringing a drill back for half a hectare.
drone-seeding.cadence: On demand, mostly cover crop establishment and repair work.
drone-seeding.readings.2: Establishment rate at the check flight
drone-seeding.steps.0.title: Plan
drone-seeding.steps.0.text: The target area comes from a boundary you draw or from the gap map produced by an earlier flight.
drone-seeding.steps.1.title: Load
drone-seeding.steps.1.text: The hopper is filled with seed or coated pods and calibrated for the rate you want.
drone-seeding.steps.2.title: Broadcast
drone-seeding.steps.2.text: The drone flies the pattern at a fixed height and speed, holding the rate across the whole area.
drone-seeding.steps.3.title: Verify
drone-seeding.steps.3.text: An establishment flight two to three weeks later counts what actually came up.

frost-protection.name: Frost protection
frost-protection.tagline: Know which hollow will freeze tonight
frost-protection.summary: Drones measure temperature across the block and identify the pockets that will drop below the damage threshold first.
frost-protection.problem: A radiation frost is not uniform. Cold air drains downhill and pools, so one corner of an orchard can sit two or three degrees below the weather station on the shed roof. Protection gets deployed on the station's reading, which means either the whole block is protected at great cost or the wrong part of it is.
frost-protection.cadence: Through the frost risk window, on every clear night with a forecast minimum near the threshold.
frost-protection.sensors.1: Calibrated air temperature probe at crop height
frost-protection.outputs.0: Cold pocket map for the block
frost-protection.readings.3: Minutes spent below threshold per pocket
frost-protection.steps.0.title: Profile
frost-protection.steps.0.text: Flights on clear cold nights build a temperature surface for the block at crop height.
frost-protection.steps.1.title: Predict
frost-protection.steps.1.text: The recorded drainage pattern is combined with the forecast to name tonight's cold pockets before dusk.
frost-protection.steps.2.title: Warn
frost-protection.steps.2.text: You get the pocket map and a lead time, so wind machines, candles or irrigation go where they will earn their cost.
frost-protection.steps.3.title: Verify
frost-protection.steps.3.text: A flight during the event records what the treated and untreated areas actually did.

pollination-support.name: Pollination support
pollination-support.tagline: Cover the gap when the bees cannot
pollination-support.summary: Small drones assist pollination indoors and in blocks where natural pollinator activity is short.
pollination-support.problem: Glasshouse crops and early flowering orchards need pollination at a moment that does not always line up with pollinator activity. Cold, wet or windy flowering weather keeps bees in, hired hives are expensive and cannot be timed precisely, and a missed window shows up directly in fruit set.
pollination-support.outputs.2: Fruit set count against reference rows
pollination-support.readings.3: Days of poor natural pollinator weather covered
pollination-support.steps.0.title: Time
pollination-support.steps.0.text: Flowering is tracked from imagery so the assist runs on the days that actually matter.
pollination-support.steps.1.title: Fly slow
pollination-support.steps.1.text: A light drone works the rows at canopy height on a repeatable path.
pollination-support.steps.2.title: Assist
pollination-support.steps.2.text: Controlled airflow moves pollen within the canopy without stripping or bruising the flowers.
pollination-support.steps.3.title: Check
pollination-support.steps.3.text: Fruit set is counted afterwards and compared against untreated reference rows.

livestock-and-fences.name: Livestock and fence checks
livestock-and-fences.tagline: The daily round without the drive
livestock-and-fences.summary: Drones walk the fence line, count the herd and flag animals that are injured, missing or lying unusually still.
livestock-and-fences.problem: Checking outlying grazing means a drive, a gate, a walk and an hour, every day, in all weather. Most days nothing is wrong. The days something is wrong, the delay between the fence going down and somebody noticing is the whole problem.
livestock-and-fences.cadence: Daily or twice daily through the grazing season.
livestock-and-fences.steps.0.title: Patrol
livestock-and-fences.steps.0.text: A fixed route covers the fence line and the grazing block on a schedule.
livestock-and-fences.steps.1.title: Count
livestock-and-fences.steps.1.text: Animals are counted and compared against the number the block should hold.
livestock-and-fences.steps.2.title: Assess
livestock-and-fences.steps.2.text: Thermal and visual signatures flag animals that are separated, lame, or lying still when the herd is grazing.
livestock-and-fences.steps.3.title: Report
livestock-and-fences.steps.3.text: A short summary lands after each patrol, with photographs of anything that needs a human decision.

bird-deterrence.name: Autonomous bird deterrence
bird-deterrence.tagline: Move the flock without living next to a gas gun
bird-deterrence.summary: Drones clear birds from ripening crops on demand, instead of a permanent noise source that birds learn to ignore.
bird-deterrence.problem: Fixed deterrents work for about a fortnight. Birds habituate to gas guns, kites and tape, then feed underneath them while the neighbours are still listening to the bangs. Damage in cherries, berries and ripening maize is concentrated in a few weeks and a few blocks.
bird-deterrence.cadence: On demand through ripening, triggered by detection rather than a timer.
bird-deterrence.outputs.0: Pressure map by block and hour
bird-deterrence.readings.1: Minutes of flock presence per block
bird-deterrence.steps.0.title: Watch
bird-deterrence.steps.0.text: Cameras on the block detect flock arrival rather than running a fixed schedule.
bird-deterrence.steps.1.title: Launch
bird-deterrence.steps.1.text: A drone lifts from the nearest station and flies the approach the flock is actually using.
bird-deterrence.steps.2.title: Move on
bird-deterrence.steps.2.text: The flock is pushed off the block on a varied path, so the pattern never becomes predictable.
bird-deterrence.steps.3.title: Log
bird-deterrence.steps.3.text: Each response is recorded, so pressure by block and time of day becomes visible over the season.

soil-compaction.name: Soil compaction detection
soil-compaction.tagline: Read the tramlines the crop is drawing for you
soil-compaction.summary: Growth patterns, imagery and machine data together show where heavy traffic has closed the soil up.
soil-compaction.problem: Compaction is invisible from the surface and expensive to find with a penetrometer, so it usually gets diagnosed years late by a crop that keeps underperforming in the same strips. Headlands, gateways and the lines a full trailer took in a wet harvest are the usual suspects, but suspicion is not a map.
soil-compaction.cadence: Once or twice per season, best read at peak biomass.
soil-compaction.readings.0: Suspected area as a share of the field
soil-compaction.steps.0.title: Overlay
soil-compaction.steps.0.text: Crop performance from multispectral flights is laid over the machine traffic your terminals recorded.
soil-compaction.steps.1.title: Correlate
soil-compaction.steps.1.text: Persistent underperformance that follows traffic lines is separated from underperformance that follows soil type.
soil-compaction.steps.2.title: Rank
soil-compaction.steps.2.text: Suspected areas are ranked by size and yield cost so the penetrometer goes to the worst first.
soil-compaction.steps.3.title: Confirm
soil-compaction.steps.3.text: Your ground measurements are recorded against each area and close the loop on the model.

sustainability-dashboard.name: Sustainability reporting
sustainability-dashboard.tagline: The paperwork writes itself from the flights
sustainability-dashboard.summary: Flight data, weather, soil and machine records combine into the input and water figures your buyers and schemes ask for.
sustainability-dashboard.problem: Reporting obligations keep growing while the underlying numbers still live in a spray diary, a fuel receipt and somebody's memory. Assembling a defensible figure for product use or water per hectare takes days, and the result is hard to audit because the evidence is scattered.
sustainability-dashboard.cadence: Continuous, with reporting periods you define.
sustainability-dashboard.sensors.0: No flight of its own: it consumes every other capability's output
sustainability-dashboard.outputs.0: Input use per hectare and per tonne
sustainability-dashboard.steps.0.title: Collect
sustainability-dashboard.steps.0.text: Every flight, prescription and as applied record is captured at the moment it happens.
sustainability-dashboard.steps.1.title: Reconcile
sustainability-dashboard.steps.1.text: Planned against applied is reconciled per field, so the numbers reflect what went on, not what was ordered.
sustainability-dashboard.steps.2.title: Aggregate
sustainability-dashboard.steps.2.text: Field figures roll up to block, farm and enterprise level with the flight evidence still attached.
sustainability-dashboard.steps.3.title: Export
sustainability-dashboard.steps.3.text: Reports export in the formats schemes and buyers accept, with the source data one click away.

drone-service.name: Flights as a service
drone-service.tagline: Book the flights, not the aircraft
drone-service.summary: You book a scouting schedule and get analysis and recommendations. We own the drones, the pilots and the paperwork.
drone-service.problem: Buying a drone means buying a training course, an operator registration, an insurance policy, a maintenance schedule and the risk that the model is obsolete in three seasons. Most farms want the map, not the aircraft, and the aircraft sits in a shed between the six weeks a year it earns anything.
drone-service.cadence: Set once per crop and adjusted as the season moves.
drone-service.steps.0.title: Scope
drone-service.steps.0.text: We walk your blocks, agree which capabilities matter and set the flight calendar around your crop.
drone-service.steps.1.title: Fly
drone-service.steps.1.text: Our pilots fly the schedule. Registration, insurance, airspace clearance and maintenance are ours.
drone-service.steps.2.title: Report
drone-service.steps.2.text: Each flight produces a report with problem areas, recommendations and the maps your machines can load.
drone-service.steps.3.title: Review
drone-service.steps.3.text: We sit down at the end of the season with what the data showed and what to change next year.

autonomous-network.name: Autonomous drone network
autonomous-network.tagline: Docked, charged, and out again at first light
autonomous-network.summary: Drones launch from charging stations on their own schedule, cover the fields and dock again without a driver.
autonomous-network.problem: A pilot in a van is the bottleneck. Travel time between blocks decides how many fields get flown in a day, which means the outlying ones get flown least and the schedule collapses the moment the weather closes a window.
autonomous-network.cadence: Daily, weather permitting, with the calendar published a week ahead.
autonomous-network.outputs.1: Missed flight report with the reason
autonomous-network.steps.0.title: Station
autonomous-network.steps.0.text: Weatherproof docks are placed to cover your blocks within a single battery.
autonomous-network.steps.1.title: Schedule
autonomous-network.steps.1.text: Each field has its own cadence; the network plans the day around weather, wind and daylight.
autonomous-network.steps.2.title: Fly and dock
autonomous-network.steps.2.text: Aircraft launch, fly their route, return and charge without anyone attending.
autonomous-network.steps.3.title: Escalate
autonomous-network.steps.3.text: Anything the models are unsure about goes to a human reviewer before it reaches you.

field-assistant.name: Field decision assistant
field-assistant.tagline: A recommendation, not another image folder
field-assistant.summary: The assistant reads every layer for a field and answers in plain language: what is wrong, where, and by when.
field-assistant.problem: More sensing produces more imagery, and imagery is not a decision. A folder of index maps and a change layer still leaves somebody to work out whether the yellow patch in the north west matters this week, and what to do about it before Thursday.
field-assistant.cadence: After every flight, plus a weekly farm level brief.
field-assistant.sensors.0: No flight of its own: it reasons over the whole field record
field-assistant.outputs.2: Evidence links back to the source flight
field-assistant.readings.3: Average lead time on a window
field-assistant.steps.0.title: Read
field-assistant.steps.0.text: Every layer for the field is read together: imagery, weather, soil, machine records and your own notes.
field-assistant.steps.1.title: Reason
field-assistant.steps.1.text: Findings are weighed against growth stage and forecast, so a flag in June is not treated like the same flag in April.
field-assistant.steps.2.title: Recommend
field-assistant.steps.2.text: You get a written recommendation naming the area, the likely cause, the action and the window.
field-assistant.steps.3.title: Follow up
field-assistant.steps.3.text: Every recommendation is tracked, and the next flight reports whether it worked.

winter-wheat.name: Winter wheat and barley
winter-wheat.tagline: The long season, flown in stages
winter-wheat.summary: Establishment gaps, patchy weed pressure, septoria risk and a nitrogen plan that has to follow the field, not a flat rate.
winter-wheat.challenge: A cereal crop is in the ground for the better part of a year and every problem in it is patchy. Blackgrass concentrates along the tramlines and headlands. Septoria starts in the thickest, wettest part of the canopy. The nitrogen plan gets split three ways and applied flat because there is no map that says otherwise. Each of those is a decision made blind, repeated across every field on the farm.
winter-wheat.approach: A base map at establishment, then a fortnightly multispectral cadence through the stem extension and flag leaf windows, tightening when the weather turns favourable for septoria. Weed scans land before each herbicide window and produce a prescription your sprayer can load. Nitrogen splits are prescribed from measured biomass rather than a target applied evenly.
winter-wheat.scale: Blocks of 10 to 120 hectares, flown as one route.
winter-wheat.outcomes.0: Treated area recorded against total area for every herbicide pass
winter-wheat.outcomes.1: Nitrogen prescribed per zone with the measured shortfall behind it
winter-wheat.outcomes.2: Disease flags dated and located, days before a cab-level diagnosis
winter-wheat.outcomes.3: A yield estimate that narrows through grain fill instead of arriving at harvest
winter-wheat.season.0.focus: Establishment counts, gap mapping and a corrected boundary for the field record.
winter-wheat.season.1.focus: Weed mapping before the autumn or spring herbicide window.
winter-wheat.season.2.focus: Biomass and chlorophyll for the first and second nitrogen split.
winter-wheat.season.3.focus: Disease surveillance on a tight cadence, plus ear counts for the yield estimate.
winter-wheat.season.4.focus: Yield forecast update, lodging map and harvest sequencing.

maize.name: Maize
maize.tagline: Early weeks decide it, and birds finish it
maize.summary: Establishment counts, early weed competition, corn borer pressure and flocks working the cobs at ripening.
maize.challenge: Maize forgives nothing in the first six weeks. A gappy stand cannot be fixed later, and weeds that get away before the canopy closes take yield directly. Then at the other end of the season, once the cobs are filling, flocks move in and a fixed deterrent stops working after a fortnight. Between those two ends the crop is too tall to walk into and too dense to see through.
maize.approach: A counting flight at the three to five leaf stage sets the establishment number and finds the gaps. Weed scans run before the post-emergence window and produce a spot-spray prescription. Once the crop is over head height, flights are the only practical way to see inside the block, so pest surveillance runs on a fixed cadence. At ripening, camera triggered deterrence responds to flocks rather than running on a timer.
maize.scale: Blocks of 5 to 80 hectares, with deterrence stations on the blocks under pressure.
maize.outcomes.0: Establishment counted rather than estimated from a pacing walk
maize.outcomes.1: Weed treatment confined to mapped zones before canopy closure
maize.outcomes.2: Pest and bird pressure logged by block and hour across the season
maize.outcomes.3: Chopping order set from measured yield, not from the gate view
maize.season.0.focus: Plant counts per square metre and the gap map.
maize.season.1.focus: Weed mapping for the post-emergence spot-spray prescription.
maize.season.2.focus: Nitrogen top-up zoning and pest surveillance from above.
maize.season.3.focus: Bird pressure monitoring and on-demand deterrence.
maize.season.4.focus: Yield estimate and lodging assessment for the chopping order.

oilseed-rape.name: Oilseed rape
oilseed-rape.tagline: Uneven from the day it goes in
oilseed-rape.summary: Patchy establishment, flea beetle damage, and a canopy that needs measuring before the nitrogen decision is worth anything.
oilseed-rape.challenge: Rape establishes unevenly and then the gaps get worse. Flea beetle damage is concentrated and easy to miss until the affected patch has thinned out entirely. Canopy size drives the whole nitrogen decision, and a canopy that varies threefold across a field makes a flat rate close to meaningless. Deciding whether to keep or redrill a struggling field is one of the more expensive calls of the year, and it is usually made from the gateway.
oilseed-rape.approach: Two establishment flights turn keep-or-redrill into a decision with an area behind it. Pest surveillance through the autumn tracks damage patches as they grow or stall. Canopy measurement before the spring nitrogen produces the zoning, with the green area index measured rather than guessed.
oilseed-rape.outcomes.0: Keep-or-redrill decided from a measured established area
oilseed-rape.outcomes.1: Damage patches tracked across flights instead of found once
oilseed-rape.outcomes.2: Spring nitrogen zoned to the measured canopy
oilseed-rape.outcomes.3: Desiccation timed by zone rather than by field
oilseed-rape.season.0.focus: Establishment counts and the keep-or-redrill area calculation.
oilseed-rape.season.1.focus: Flea beetle damage tracking, patch by patch.
oilseed-rape.season.2.focus: Canopy measurement for the spring nitrogen zoning.
oilseed-rape.season.3.focus: Uniformity check and disease surveillance through the risk window.
oilseed-rape.season.4.focus: Yield estimate and desiccation timing by zone.

sugar-beet.name: Sugar beet
sugar-beet.summary: Wide rows and slow early growth make beet the crop where weed mapping and spot treatment save the most.
sugar-beet.challenge: Beet sits in wide rows and grows slowly at first, so bare soil stays exposed for weeks and weeds have an open run at it. The herbicide programme is repeated and expensive, and it is applied across the whole field because the actual weed distribution has never been mapped. Beet is also a heavy crop moved by heavy machines, so the compaction from last year's lifting shows up in this year's stand.
sugar-beet.approach: Weed scans ahead of every pass in the programme, producing a prescription per pass rather than a single map for the season. Compaction analysis reads the crop over the traffic lines your terminals recorded. A base elevation map handles the standing water that beet punishes hardest.
sugar-beet.outcomes.0: A prescription per herbicide pass rather than one blanket rate
sugar-beet.outcomes.1: Treated area recorded pass by pass across the programme
sugar-beet.outcomes.2: Compaction located against recorded machine traffic
sugar-beet.outcomes.3: Standing water areas mapped from the elevation model
sugar-beet.season.0.focus: Establishment counts and the first weed map before the herbicide programme starts.
sugar-beet.season.1.focus: A fresh weed map before each pass, exported as a prescription.
sugar-beet.season.2.focus: Foliar disease surveillance and nitrogen top-up zoning.
sugar-beet.season.3.focus: Compaction analysis over recorded traffic and the yield estimate.
sugar-beet.season.4.focus: Traffic damage map for next season's remediation plan.

potatoes.name: Potatoes
potatoes.tagline: Blight, irrigation and a crop you cannot see
potatoes.summary: Blight surveillance on a tight cadence, irrigation uniformity from thermal imaging, and a yield estimate before lifting.
potatoes.challenge: Potatoes carry two problems at once. Late blight moves fast enough that a few days of delay changes the outcome, and the standard answer is a protective spray programme applied across everything on a calendar. Irrigation is the other: a blocked nozzle or an under-delivering arc runs for weeks while the crop underneath quietly fails, and none of it is visible from the headland.
potatoes.approach: Multispectral flights on a short cadence through the blight risk window, always compared against the field's own history rather than an absolute threshold. Thermal flights during the irrigation season locate leaks and dry patches to a coordinate. A counting flight before lifting gives the estimate that the storage and haulage booking depends on.
potatoes.scale: Blocks of 5 to 60 hectares, usually irrigated.
potatoes.outcomes.0: Blight flags dated and located, with the change since the last flight attached
potatoes.outcomes.1: Irrigation anomalies given coordinates instead of a general area
potatoes.outcomes.2: Water applied recorded per irrigated hectare
potatoes.outcomes.3: Storage and haulage booked against a measured estimate
potatoes.season.1.focus: Nitrogen zoning and the first irrigation uniformity check.
potatoes.season.2.focus: Short cadence disease surveillance with a change layer per flight.
potatoes.season.3.focus: Thermal irrigation flights fortnightly, plus a check after every repair.
potatoes.season.4.focus: Yield estimate and the haulm destruction plan by zone.

vineyards.name: Vineyards
vineyards.tagline: Steep ground, tight rows, high value
vineyards.summary: Vigour mapping by row, downy and powdery mildew surveillance, frost pockets, and the terrain where drone application is actually permitted.
vineyards.challenge: A vineyard is the same plants for thirty years, which makes every uneven patch a compounding problem rather than a one-season one. Vigour varies row by row and often vine by vine. Mildew pressure builds inside a canopy that nobody can see into from outside. And on steep sites the machinery that can legally treat the crop is limited by the slope itself, which is precisely the terrain where the EU permits aerial application by exemption.
vineyards.approach: Row-resolution vigour mapping that reports per row and per panel, not per block average. Disease surveillance timed to the infection periods rather than a calendar. Frost profiling across the site through spring, because cold air pooling in a vineyard is repeatable and therefore predictable. On steep parcels where the exemption applies, application follows the same maps.
vineyards.scale: Parcels of 0.5 to 20 hectares, including slopes machinery cannot work.
vineyards.outcomes.0: Vigour reported per row and per panel, not as a block average
vineyards.outcomes.1: Mildew surveillance tied to infection periods with dated evidence
vineyards.outcomes.2: Cold pockets named before dusk rather than diagnosed after sunrise
vineyards.outcomes.3: Harvest sequencing built from measured ripeness variation
vineyards.season.0.focus: Frost pocket profiling and the overnight risk brief on clear nights.
vineyards.season.1.focus: Vigour mapping by row for canopy management and pruning decisions.
vineyards.season.2.focus: Mildew surveillance timed to infection periods.
vineyards.season.3.focus: Water status by thermal imaging and the harvest sequencing map.
vineyards.season.4.focus: Missing and declining vine census for replanting.

orchards.name: Orchards
orchards.tagline: Count the fruit, protect the blossom
orchards.summary: Fruit counting for the pack house booking, blossom frost protection, tree by tree health, and birds at ripening.
orchards.challenge: An orchard's year turns on two short windows. A frost during blossom can remove the crop in a single night, and protection is expensive enough that it needs to go exactly where the cold actually collects. Then at harvest, the pack house, the labour and the storage all need a number weeks ahead, and that number traditionally comes from counting a few trees and multiplying. Between those, individual trees decline, and a declining tree in row 14 looks like every other tree from the end of the row.
orchards.approach: Frost profiling through blossom, with a nightly brief when the forecast is near the threshold. Fruit counting flights at set points after fruit set, aggregated per row and per block. Tree by tree health tracking that carries an identity across seasons, so decline is a trend rather than a discovery.
orchards.outcomes.0: Frost protection deployed to mapped cold pockets
orchards.outcomes.1: Pack house and labour booked against counted fruit
orchards.outcomes.2: Individual trees tracked across seasons rather than sampled
orchards.outcomes.3: Picking sequenced from measured ripeness by row
orchards.season.0.focus: Frost pocket mapping and nightly risk briefs.
orchards.season.1.focus: Set counts against reference rows and the first crop estimate.
orchards.season.2.focus: Tree by tree health tracking, irrigation uniformity, canopy vigour.
orchards.season.3.focus: Fruit counts per row, sizing estimate and picking sequence.
orchards.season.4.focus: Bird pressure monitoring and on-demand deterrence.

berries.name: Soft fruit and berries
berries.tagline: High value per square metre, short windows
berries.summary: Picking forecasts for labour planning, irrigation uniformity under tunnels, bird pressure and frost on early varieties.
berries.challenge: Soft fruit is the crop where a scheduling mistake costs the most per hectare. Pickers are booked days ahead against a forecast, and a forecast that is out by a quarter means either fruit left on the plant or a crew standing idle. Under tunnels, irrigation problems compound quickly because there is no rainfall to mask them. Birds take a meaningful share in the fortnight before picking.
berries.approach: Frequent counting flights through ripening so the picking forecast is updated rather than set once. Thermal irrigation checks on the tunnel blocks, where a blocked line shows within days. Detection-triggered bird deterrence rather than a permanent noise source next to a public road.
berries.scale: Blocks of 0.5 to 15 hectares, open field and tunnels.
berries.outcomes.0: Picking crews booked against a forecast that updates through ripening
berries.outcomes.1: Irrigation faults under tunnels found in days rather than weeks
berries.outcomes.2: Bird response logged by block and hour instead of running continuously
berries.outcomes.3: Plant replacement lists built from a census, not a walk
berries.season.0.focus: Frost risk profiling on early varieties.
berries.season.1.focus: Pollination assist on poor weather days and fruit set counts.
berries.season.2.focus: Irrigation uniformity under tunnels and canopy health.
berries.season.3.focus: Counting flights for the picking forecast and active bird deterrence.
berries.season.4.focus: Plant health census and replacement planting list.

hops.name: Hops
hops.tagline: A wall of canopy you cannot see into
hops.summary: Downy mildew and spider mite surveillance from above, plus vigour mapping across a trellis that hides everything at ground level.
hops.challenge: A hop yard in July is a seven metre wall of canopy. Walking it tells you about the outside row and almost nothing about the middle of the block. Downy mildew and spider mite both start in pockets, and both are far cheaper to deal with early. The crop is high value, the treatment programme is intensive, and the whole thing is applied on the assumption that the block is uniform.
hops.approach: Overhead multispectral flights read the canopy the ground crew cannot reach, on a cadence tight enough to catch a pocket while it is still a pocket. Vigour mapping runs by row and by bine position. Findings are ranked into a scouting route so the crew walks to the worst rows first rather than sampling.
hops.outcomes.0: The middle of the block surveyed as often as the edge rows
hops.outcomes.1: Scouting routed to ranked areas rather than sampled at random
hops.outcomes.2: Nitrogen zoned to measured vigour by row
hops.outcomes.3: Contract volumes estimated from counted cones
hops.season.0.focus: Establishment and bine count per hill.
hops.season.1.focus: Vigour mapping by row and nitrogen zoning.
hops.season.2.focus: Mildew and mite surveillance on a tight cadence, ranked scouting routes.
hops.season.3.focus: Health surveillance and the yield estimate for the contract.
hops.season.4.focus: Picking sequence by block from measured maturity.

grassland-and-hay.name: Grassland and silage
grassland-and-hay.summary: Thermal fawn searches ahead of first cut, sward quality mapping, and reseeding where the ground has gone back.
grassland-and-hay.challenge: First cut silage is the single most lethal operation of the farming year for wildlife. Roe deer leave fawns lying in tall grass and a fawn will press flat rather than run from a mower. In Germany the duty to take reasonable precautions falls on whoever is doing the mowing, and a line of volunteers walking a 12 hectare field before dawn is neither reliable nor repeatable. Separately, sward quality drifts: patches go back to weed grasses and nobody maps it until the analysis comes back poor.
grassland-and-hay.approach: A thermal search flown in the cool hours before the mower starts, with finds pushed live to the phone of whoever is on the ground, and a coverage record kept per field. Sward composition is mapped between cuts so reseeding is targeted. Drone broadcast handles the wet hollows and steep banks a machine should not be on.
grassland-and-hay.scale: Fields of 2 to 40 hectares, flown at dawn.
grassland-and-hay.outcomes.0: A search record per field, signed off before the mower starts
grassland-and-hay.outcomes.1: Finds logged with coordinates and outcome
grassland-and-hay.outcomes.2: Reseeding targeted at mapped thin areas
grassland-and-hay.outcomes.3: Cut yields estimated rather than counted off the clamp
grassland-and-hay.season.0.focus: Thermal wildlife search with live find marking and a coverage record.
grassland-and-hay.season.1.focus: Sward quality and weed grass mapping.
grassland-and-hay.season.2.focus: Repeat searches on fields with known activity, plus yield estimates per cut.
grassland-and-hay.season.3.focus: Overseeding of thin areas by drone where machinery cannot travel.
grassland-and-hay.season.4.focus: Drainage and wet area mapping for the winter works list.

dairy-pasture.name: Dairy and grazing livestock
dairy-pasture.tagline: The outlying block, checked every morning
dairy-pasture.summary: Daily head counts, fence line inspection and flagged animals, without the drive to every outlying block.
dairy-pasture.challenge: The blocks furthest from the yard get checked least, and they are the ones where a fence going down matters most. A daily round of outlying grazing is an hour of driving that finds nothing on most days. On the days it would have found something, the delay between the event and the check is the whole cost: an animal through a fence onto a road, or a cow down in a corner since the previous evening.
dairy-pasture.approach: A scheduled patrol per block, flown from a dock rather than driven to. Head count against expected, fence line imagery, and thermal signatures that separate an animal lying and ruminating from an animal lying and not. Anything ambiguous goes to a person before it becomes an alert.
dairy-pasture.scale: Grazing platforms of 20 to 300 hectares, docks placed by battery range.
dairy-pasture.outcomes.0: Head count per block recorded daily against expected
dairy-pasture.outcomes.1: Fence faults reported the morning they appear
dairy-pasture.outcomes.2: Flagged animals delivered with imagery for a human decision
dairy-pasture.outcomes.3: Grazing rotation planned from mapped cover
dairy-pasture.season.0.focus: Fence line survey of every block before stock go out.
dairy-pasture.season.1.focus: Daily patrols with head counts and flagged animal reports.
dairy-pasture.season.2.focus: Grass cover mapping for the grazing rotation.
dairy-pasture.season.3.focus: Poaching and damage mapping for the reseeding plan.
dairy-pasture.season.4.focus: Fence and water point condition survey for the winter works list.

organic-farms.name: Organic farms
organic-farms.tagline: Mechanical weeding needs a map more than anyone
organic-farms.summary: Without herbicides, weed location decides where the hoe goes, when, and how many passes the field actually needs.
organic-farms.challenge: An organic rotation has no rescue treatment, so timing is everything and the tool is mechanical. Hoeing and harrowing are expensive in fuel, time and soil disturbance, and they get run across the whole field because the weed distribution is unknown. Run too early and the weeds return; too late and the crop takes the damage. Meanwhile nutrient supply comes from the rotation and manure, both of which vary across a field far more than a bought fertiliser does.
organic-farms.approach: Weed mapping ahead of each mechanical pass, which turns a whole-field operation into a targeted one and often removes a pass entirely. Nutrient status is measured rather than assumed, so manure and compost go where the rotation has left a gap. Cover crop establishment is verified by counting rather than by eye.
organic-farms.outcomes.0: Mechanical passes targeted to mapped areas, with passes saved recorded
organic-farms.outcomes.1: Manure and compost placed against measured shortfall
organic-farms.outcomes.2: Cover crop establishment counted, not assumed
organic-farms.outcomes.3: Certification evidence assembled from flight records
organic-farms.season.0.focus: Weed burden mapping and the seedbed plan.
organic-farms.season.1.focus: Weed maps before each hoeing or harrowing pass.
organic-farms.season.2.focus: Nutrient status mapping for targeted manure and compost.
organic-farms.season.3.focus: Yield estimate and a weed seed return map for the rotation plan.
organic-farms.season.4.focus: Cover crop broadcast and an establishment count two weeks later.

greenhouses.name: Glasshouses and protected crops
greenhouses.tagline: Indoors, where the weather never helps
greenhouses.summary: Pollination assist through flowering, canopy health by row, and irrigation uniformity across a house with no rain to mask it.
greenhouses.challenge: A glasshouse removes the weather and with it the pollinators, the natural water and the margin for error. Hired hives are expensive and cannot be timed to a specific week. Irrigation problems compound within days because nothing else waters the crop. And because the crop is uniform by design, a problem that starts in one row is easy to miss until it is in twenty.
greenhouses.approach: Small indoor aircraft on a fixed path per house. Pollination assist runs through the flowering window on the days natural activity would be poor. Canopy health is read row by row so an early divergence is visible while it is still one row. Irrigation uniformity is checked on a schedule rather than after a problem appears.
greenhouses.scale: Houses of 0.2 to 10 hectares under glass or plastic.
greenhouses.outcomes.0: Pollination covered on the days natural activity would not be
greenhouses.outcomes.1: Fruit set counted against untreated reference rows
greenhouses.outcomes.2: Row level divergence caught while it is still one row
greenhouses.outcomes.3: Picking and packing planned against counted fruit
greenhouses.season.0.focus: Row by row establishment record for the house.
greenhouses.season.1.focus: Daily pollination assist and fruit set counts against reference rows.
greenhouses.season.2.focus: Canopy health by row and irrigation uniformity checks.
greenhouses.season.3.focus: Counting flights for the picking and packing forecast.
greenhouses.season.4.focus: End of cycle health census and a plan for the next planting.

contractors.name: Agricultural contractors
contractors.tagline: A service you can resell by the hectare
contractors.summary: Add scouting, wildlife searches and prescription maps to the work you already do, without buying a fleet.
contractors.challenge: A contractor already owns the machines, the operators and the customer relationships. What they do not own is a reason for the customer to pay for anything beyond the pass itself. Meanwhile the mowing they do on contract carries the wildlife obligation, and the spraying they do is applied flat because the customer has no map. Both are liabilities that could be services.
contractors.approach: Contractors run the flights as part of the job: a wildlife search flown before the mower goes in, a weed map before the sprayer, and a prescription that loads straight into the machine already on the yard. The reports carry the contractor's name and become the record the customer keeps.
contractors.scale: Portfolios of 500 to 5,000 hectares across many holdings.
contractors.outcomes.0: Search and treatment records held per customer and per field
contractors.outcomes.1: Prescriptions delivered in the format the customer's terminal expects
contractors.outcomes.2: Hectares flown tracked against hectares worked
contractors.outcomes.3: A billable service attached to passes that were previously flat rate
contractors.season.0.focus: Wildlife searches ahead of every first cut on the books.
contractors.season.1.focus: Weed maps and prescriptions ahead of each spraying job.
contractors.season.2.focus: Variable rate prescriptions for the spreading work.
contractors.season.3.focus: Yield estimates that set the trailer and haulage plan per customer.
contractors.season.4.focus: Season reviews per customer and next year's flight calendar.

cooperatives.name: Cooperatives and large estates
cooperatives.tagline: One picture across every member holding
cooperatives.summary: Fleet coverage across scattered blocks, comparable numbers between holdings, and reporting that rolls up cleanly.
cooperatives.challenge: A cooperative or a large estate has the same problem repeated dozens of times, plus one of its own: nothing is comparable. Each holding records differently, applies differently and reports differently, so an aggregate figure is either unavailable or not defensible. The blocks are scattered, which makes a pilot in a van an expensive way to cover them.
cooperatives.approach: Docked aircraft placed to cover clusters of blocks, flying a schedule instead of a route driven by travel time. Every holding is measured the same way, so member comparison and benchmarking are meaningful. Reporting rolls up from field to holding to enterprise with the source flight still attached to each figure.
cooperatives.scale: 2,000 to 40,000 hectares across scattered member blocks.
cooperatives.outcomes.0: Every holding measured the same way, so comparison means something
cooperatives.outcomes.1: Coverage set by schedule rather than by driving distance
cooperatives.outcomes.2: Aggregate reporting with the source flight attached to each figure
cooperatives.outcomes.3: Marketing and logistics planned from estimates that update weekly
cooperatives.season.0.focus: Base mapping across every member block and a shared field register.
cooperatives.season.1.focus: Scheduled coverage from docks, with a published weekly calendar.
cooperatives.season.2.focus: Prescriptions distributed to each holding's machines.
cooperatives.season.3.focus: Yield estimates aggregated for the marketing and logistics plan.
cooperatives.season.4.focus: Input, water and treated area reporting rolled up with evidence.

reforestation.name: Reforestation and land restoration
reforestation.tagline: Plant the slope nobody can walk
reforestation.summary: Terrain mapping, seed pod broadcast onto ground machines cannot reach, and establishment counts that prove it worked.
reforestation.challenge: Restoration work happens on exactly the ground that is hardest to work: steep slopes, burnt or storm damaged stands, wet ground and sites with no access track. Hand planting is slow and dangerous there. And once seed is in, the follow-up question, whether anything actually established, is usually answered by a walk over a small sample and a hopeful extrapolation.
reforestation.approach: A terrain survey first, so the planting plan follows slope, aspect and drainage rather than a shape on a map. Seed pods are broadcast at a controlled rate over the areas machines cannot reach. Establishment flights at fixed intervals count what came up, and the gaps become the next broadcast's target area.
reforestation.scale: Sites of 1 to 500 hectares, including terrain with no vehicle access.
reforestation.outcomes.0: Planting planned against measured slope, aspect and drainage
reforestation.outcomes.1: As-applied coverage recorded for every broadcast
reforestation.outcomes.2: Establishment and survival counted at fixed intervals
reforestation.outcomes.3: Follow-up broadcasts targeted at mapped gaps
reforestation.season.0.focus: Terrain model, slope and aspect analysis, and the planting plan.
reforestation.season.1.focus: Seed pod application at the planned rate, with an as-applied coverage map.
reforestation.season.2.focus: First establishment count and the gap map.
reforestation.season.3.focus: Survival count and the target area for the follow-up broadcast.
reforestation.season.4.focus: Annual canopy development tracking against the restoration plan.
